records.title: Expert runtime: Common Lisp Tek9 store + typed Prolog shim
Post-merge findings from #1147: compaction result-summary check fails open on NULL, plus two unguarded recursive CTEs
records.body:
Four Codex findings on #1147 ("Bound successor context-compaction validation") are dispositioned here. Two arrived in a review **body** with no inline thread; two were unresolved inline threads. All four are on the merged migration `crates/persistence/migrations/202608210615_bound_successor_compaction_validation.sql`.

**Provenance.** The migration blob is `28b69156ec2a77796da3869c01a6a33780f61324` at the reviewed commit `25b7717d63`, at `79825b423`, and at `origin/main` `aef3fecf5` — `git diff 25b7717d63 origin/main -- <file>` is empty. No later migration redefines any of the three functions: `context_frontier_member_position` is defined once (0615:4), `context_frontier_preserves_prefix` last at 0615:51, `require_context_compaction_exact_evidence` last at 0615:110. Migrations are append-only here, so redefinition was the only route to a cure and there is none. **All four are real on `main`.**

**Reachability, stated up front.** None of the four is reachable through the Rust persistence crate. Frontier prefixes always point at an already-committed frontier and the result frontier is written before the compaction row (`crates/persistence/src/context_compaction.rs:521` then `:544`); `predecessor_compaction_id` is derived server-side as the session's successor-less leaf (`:1080-1097`) with a fresh UUID; foreign-session frontier members are unmintable today; and production appends exactly the summary to the result frontier. All four need a hand-crafted transaction. That is why none of them is P1.

**Fix order: 3, then 1, then 4, then 2.** Finding 3 is the only one that silently weakened an invariant that previously held on `main`.

---

## 1. `context_frontier_member_position` walks prefixes with `UNION ALL` and no cycle guard

Review body, Codex P2, `202608210615...sql:19`. **Real. P3.**

`0615:14-38` recurses on `prefix_context_frontier_id` through `UNION ALL` with no visited set and no depth bound. The outer `LIMIT 1` at `:46` does not rescue it: verified on PostgreSQL 18.4 that a bare `LIMIT 1` short-circuits when a match exists but spins indefinitely when it does not — exactly the condition the finding named ("if the requested member is absent from the cyclic deltas").

The cycle is structurally admissible. `context_frontier_prefix_fk` is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` (`202607260300_context_frontier_prefixes.sql:9-15`) with no CHECK forbidding self- or mutual reference, and the rejecting trigger `context_frontier_requires_complete_membership` is deferred in the same class (`202607180004_turn_lifecycle_storage.sql:746-750`), not IMMEDIATE. Deferred constraint triggers fire in row-insertion order (verified empirically), so a transaction queuing the compaction row before the cyclic headers gets the compaction trigger first. The finding's ordering premise is correct.

**The sharpest point the reviewer did not make:** this is the only unguarded prefix walk of four in the schema. `context_frontier_preserves_prefix` — *in this same file*, at `0615:67` — uses `UNION` (dedup, cycle-safe). `resolve_context_frontier_members` (`202607260300:109`) uses `UNION`. `assert_context_frontier_complete_membership` (`202607260300:260-293`) carries an explicit `visited` array plus a `cycle` flag. The codebase already treats prefix cycles as a hazard; 0615 introduced the one walk that omits the guard. That inconsistency, not the DoS, is the reason to fix it.

## 2. Consumed-summary detection is scoped to `NEW.session`

Review body, Codex P1, `202608210615...sql:349-353`. **Real as SQL; premise unreachable today. P3.**

The scoping claim is exactly right. `0615:343-358` gates the consumed-summary lookup on `AND NEW.through_source_session_id = NEW.session_id` (`:352`), so a foreign-session summary can never be recognized as consumed. Same pattern at `0615:314-321` and `0615:389-395`.

It is also internally inconsistent: the *root* branch of this same function (`0615:203-209`) joins summaries with no session restriction, and `load_projected_frontier_members` (`crates/persistence/src/context_compaction.rs:1284-1297`) has no `source_session_id` filter either — it treats any `payload_kind = 'context_summary'` as a summary. Three of four sites are session-agnostic; only consumed-detection is scoped.

**But nothing can mint a foreign-session frontier member today.** `context_frontier_delta` has no constraint tying `source_session_id` to `owning_session_id` (its only FK on those columns targets `semantic_transcript_entry`, `202607180004:323-331`), so the reviewer is right at the schema level. The paths, however, are all closed: import seed explicitly forbids foreign members (`202607240002_imported_session_seed.sql:765`) and re-mints entries natively; an imported transcript cannot carry a `context_summary` at all (payload-shape CHECK, `202607290401:414-415`); delegation does not inherit parent entries (`202608020018:5668-5673`); and the one design that would produce foreign members — native fork, `TranscriptAncestry::SingleSource` / INV-030 (`crates/domain/src/session.rs:1588-1612`) — is not persistable, since `session_ancestry_kind_closed` (`202607240002:28-34`) admits only `'none'` and `'imported_conversation'`.

So this is forward-looking hardening that becomes load-bearing the moment INV-030 forks are persistable. The tail the reviewer describes is confirmed: if such a compaction did commit, `project_frontier_members` (`context_compaction.rs:1367-1372`) returns `ContextCompactionCorruption::Inconsistent("context summary through endpoint")` and the session's projection fails permanently. Cheap insurance: match on `consumed_summary.session_id = NEW.through_source_session_id` instead of the current-session equality.

## 3. The result-summary check fails open on NULL — a regression this PR introduced

Unresolved thread, Codex P1, `202608210615...sql:432`. https://github.com/KeenWill/signalbox/pull/1147#discussion_r3858122198 · **Real, mechanically proven, and the one worth fixing first. P2.**

records.title: bug(module-finder): guard recursive scans against symlink directory cycles
records.body:
## Priority: P1

## Summary

`src/module_finder.rs::scan_directory_inner` intentionally follows symlinked directories, but unlike `src/drift.rs` it does not track canonical directories that have already been visited.

A symlink cycle can therefore recurse indefinitely until stack exhaustion or path-length/filesystem failure.

## Evidence on current `main` (`fc53e107`)

The module finder explicitly follows symlinks:

```rust
if raw_ft.is_symlink() {
    let Ok(meta) = path.metadata() else { continue };
    effective_is_dir = meta.is_dir();
    effective_is_file = meta.is_file();
}
```

If the symlink resolves to a directory, that path is queued in `subdirs` and recursively scanned.

The existing Unix tests explicitly require symlinked package directories to be followed, so simply ignoring all directory symlinks would be a regression.

By contrast, `src/drift.rs::collect_py_files` already solved the same class of problem by maintaining a `HashSet<PathBuf>` of canonical directory paths and skipping paths already visited.

## Reproduction shape

On Unix:

```text
root/
└── pkg/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── loop -> ../pkg
```

Then:

```bash
pybun module-find --scan -p root
```

The recursive traversal can repeatedly visit:

```text
root/pkg
root/pkg/loop
root/pkg/loop/loop
root/pkg/loop/loop/loop
...
```

The exact terminal failure can depend on OS/filesystem limits, but the traversal has no cycle-breaking invariant.

## Impact

- Untrusted or unusual project trees can hang/crash `module-find --scan`.
- Editable installs and development trees commonly contain symlinks, so following symlinks is useful and should remain supported.
- If the Rust finder is later connected to normal `pybun run` import execution (#403), this becomes a runtime stability risk rather than a standalone CLI edge case.
- Parallel top-level scanning can make cyclic traversal consume additional threads/resources before failing.

## Proposed fix

Use canonical-path cycle detection, similar to the implementation already present in `src/drift.rs`:

1. Canonicalize the root and add it to a shared/local visited set.
2. Before recursing into a directory (especially a symlinked directory), canonicalize it.
3. Skip recursion when the canonical path has already been visited.
4. Preserve the module entry itself when appropriate; only suppress repeated descent.
5. Define behavior for canonicalization errors (skip with optional diagnostic rather than panic).

Because `scan_directory_inner` can dispatch top-level recursion across threads, the visited-set design must be safe for parallel branches. Options include:

- pre-resolving/deduplicating top-level canonical subdirectories before spawning;
- a shared synchronized set;
- limiting symlink-following recursion to a cycle-safe sequential helper.

## Regression tests

Add Unix tests for:

### Self-cycle

```text
pkg/loop -> pkg
```

Assert scan terminates and does not emit an unbounded number of modules.

### Parent-cycle

```text
a/b/back -> a
```

Assert traversal terminates.

### Legitimate symlink

Keep/extend the existing test proving a symlink to a real external package directory is still discovered.

### Duplicate aliases

Two symlinks pointing to the same target should have explicitly defined behavior: either both top-level aliases are represented while target recursion is bounded, or canonical deduplication is documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Directory symlink cycles cannot cause unbounded recursion.
- [ ] Existing support for legitimate symlinked package directories remains functional.
- [ ] Cycle detection works in both sequential and parallel scan paths.
- [ ] No raw panic/stack overflow occurs for cyclic trees.
- [ ] Regression tests cover self-cycle, parent-cycle, and legitimate symlink cases.

## Related

`src/drift.rs` already contains a canonical-directory visited-set pattern for this exact risk. This issue is about applying equivalent protection to `ModuleFinder`.

records.title: program(compiler-interprocedural): compose callable semantics across bounded project call graphs
records.body:
Post-upstream compiler horizon: #12514
Canonical upstream semantic bridge: #12475
Witness-backed value/flow/effect semantics: #12525
Canonical binding/place/alias/storage authority: #6659
Accepted callable-result query programme: #7433
Canonical PIR CFG and call-graph authority: #2347
CompilerWorld and project invalidation: #12527
Dynamic-boundary authority: #6683
Compile-time effect authority: #4810
Canonical semantic fact/query port: #4799
Transformation and explanation consumers: #12575 / #12616–#12624 / #12577
Independent proof, performance, status and topology: #12529 / #12531 / #12532 / #12411 / #12634

Research basis: `main@69af070b91ecc56c85fe21c712f480a8adf93ef5`; recheck current source and authority at implementation start.

## Controller only

This programme owns the missing compiler-wide join between **current callable-local semantic facts** and **bounded project-wide interprocedural answers**. **Do not open an implementation PR directly against this controller.**

The repository already has or separately owns:

```text
binding/place/storage/alias relations
program-point values and type state
callable exit/result relations and accepted direct-call queries
PIR control-flow and call-graph identity
compile-time effects and CompilerWorld dependency/currentness
explicit dynamic, XS, eval, source-filter and ambient boundaries
```

Do not recreate any of those authorities here.

The missing capability is to compose their exact current outputs across admitted call edges so the compiler can answer, without provider-local scans or arbitrary execution:

```text
what values may this call return here?
what places may it read, write, alias, localize or expose?
what warnings, exceptions, exits or external effects may propagate?
which facts remain exact through one call or a bounded recursive component?
which callers and transformed facts become stale after a callee-only change?
which internal transformations, diagnostics and bounded executions are now legal?
where does dynamic Perl force an exact refusal or conservative residual fact?
```

## Destination

```text
current canonical callable-local facts
+ exact call/caller/callee/input/context/profile subject
+ canonical PIR/CompilerWorld call edges
→ immutable callable semantic-summary references
→ direct call-site fact composition
→ bounded monotone recursive-component closure
→ exact current CompilerWorld publication and invalidation
→ independently proven analysis/diagnostic/EIR/transformation consumers
→ correctness-bound work, reuse and maintained routes
```

This is not a whole-program points-to engine or a general Perl interpreter. It is a bounded composition layer over facts whose producers and limits are already canonical.

## Imported authorities

| Concern | Existing owner retained |
|---|---|
| declaration, binding, place, access, alias, localize and capture identity | #6659 |
| context, value, control/data flow, effects and bounded evaluation | #12525 |
| callable exits, result relations, callsite inputs and accepted result query | #7433 |
| PIR CFG, call edges, control identity and future SCC substrate | #2347 |
| module/project dependency graph, CompilerWorld and exact invalidation | #12527 |
| compile-phase effects | #4810 |
| dynamic/XS/eval/source-filter/runtime boundaries | #6683 |
| provider-neutral fact/query publication | #4799 |
| transform laws/plans/equivalence | #12575 / #12616–#12624 |
| explanations | #12577 |
| upstream witnesses and independent mutation proof | #12475 / #12529 |

Compile-time effects and runtime callable effects remain distinct. A call summary may reference both where exact, but it cannot collapse their phase, source-order or currentness identities.

# PR train

## I01 — summary and application contract

`contract(compiler-interprocedural): define callable semantic summaries and call-application subjects`

Define one versioned envelope that references canonical result, effect, place/alias/escape, exceptional-control and boundary facts under exact callable/candidate/profile/currentness identity. Define direct-application, recursive-closure and refusal result semantics. No fact extraction or graph traversal.

## I02 — canonical summary assembly

`feat(compiler-interprocedural): assemble callable summaries from canonical semantic facts`

Assemble one immutable callable summary from existing current local facts and completeness/boundary evidence. No source rescan, no new effect/alias vocabulary, no callsite application.

## I03 — exact direct-call composition

`feat(compiler-interprocedural): compose result, effect, escape, and exceptional-control facts at exact direct calls`

Consume the accepted #7433 call target/input/result route and apply the exact I02 summary at one admitted direct call. Preserve argument/receiver/context/place substitution, order, provenance, uncertainty and useful work. No recursion solver.

## I04 — bounded recursive closure

`feat(compiler-interprocedural): solve recursive call components with bounded monotone closure`

Consume canonical #2347/#12527 graph and component identities. Solve only registered monotone summary facets under deterministic convergence, widening and resource policy. Dynamic or non-monotone facets remain typed boundaries. No time-based correctness and no second call graph.

## I05 — CompilerWorld publication and currentness

`feat(compiler-interprocedural): publish composed callable facts through canonical CompilerWorld queries`

Publish exact direct and recursive results through existing fact/query/currentness authorities. Callee-only changes invalidate exact dependent callers; unaffected summaries retain identity only through checked dependency equality. No provider output.

## I06 — independent semantic proof

`test(compiler-interprocedural): prove callable composition from upstream witnesses and mutations`

Use original/minimized upstream witnesses, independently authored summary and call-application expectations, ordinary changed-shape controls,

records.title: B1.3 repo-contract: compile a bounded material ArchitectureKnowledgePacket and verify it
records.body:
## Parent

#940 — trusted RepositoryContract and architecture knowledge.

Roadmap: #945 B1.3.

## Dependencies

- #968 — explicit repository-controlled contract source ingestion.
- #973/#974 — mechanically authoritative current-revision changed files, packages, targets, tests, consumers and bounded reverse dependencies.

This issue does **not** depend on the complete #927/#975 MaterialChangeMap. #975 later projects the resulting architecture/mirror/trust/support relations back into the full material map. Requiring full #927 here would create a cycle:

```text
#969 architecture packet
→ #975 full material map
→ #969 architecture packet
```

The selected seam is mechanical scope first, architecture enrichment second, full joined material map third.

## Objective

Project the durable RepositoryContract into one bounded current-run `ArchitectureKnowledgePacket` scoped by current mechanical material facts and shared by proof routing, programme selection and final review.

## Scope

- Select RepositoryContract entries using #973/#974 current changed paths/packages/targets/tests/consumers, direct ownership, bounded reverse dependencies, explicit operator scope and unresolved current source conflicts.
- Preserve authority class, source provenance/location/digest, conflicts, supersession, evidence gaps, omissions and truncation decisions.
- Keep canonical implementation, ownership, generated/source mirror, schema/verifier, test-oracle, workflow trust, compatibility and support entries separately typed.
- Emit stable section/order/source digests and one bounded prompt/proof-friendly representation.
- Prioritize higher-authority and directly material entries before lower-authority or indirectly related context.
- Represent entries that imply additional architecture/trust/support material edges as packet facts for #975; do not mutate or claim the complete MaterialChangeMap here.
- Keep model-inferred candidates clearly separate and non-authoritative.
- Add independent verifier recomputation, root/path/privacy/size constraints and stale-source rejection.
- Preserve current shared context/proof/programme behavior; emit the packet in shadow.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Relevant canonical boundaries, owners, mirrors, schema/verifier relations, test contracts, workflow trust surfaces and support promises reach the packet when triggered by #973/#974 material facts.
- [ ] Irrelevant repository corpus is excluded rather than bulk copied.
- [ ] Directly material/high-authority entries survive before lower-value context under the bound.
- [ ] Conflicts and supersession remain explicit; no parser/model silently selects a winner.
- [ ] Every packet entry traces to exact current-revision source identity and authority.
- [ ] Missing/ambiguous mechanical scope or contract source remains an explicit gap and cannot produce a false precise route.
- [ ] Model-inferred candidates cannot become Required policy or structural authority.
- [ ] Packet replay is deterministic under file/source ordering changes.
- [ ] Forged/stale source links, path escape, private/unallowlisted source and silent truncation fail verification.
- [ ] The packet exposes typed edge inputs sufficient for #975 without creating a second MaterialChangeMap.
- [ ] No proof selection, programme routing, prompt execution, scheduler, gate or public-review behavior changes.

## Proof

- Materially scoped source/test/workflow/schema/generated/multi-package goldens using #973/#974 inputs.
- Ownership, mirror, test, trust, support and compatibility contract fixtures from #968.
- Conflict/supersession, missing-scope, ambiguous-trigger and evidence-gap cases.
- Truncation priority, privacy/path/size and unallowlisted-source negatives.
- Model-inferred no-authority fixture.
- Deterministic packet/source-manifest replay and verifier forgery tests.
- #975 adapter fixture proving architecture edges can be consumed without a dependency cycle.
- Full contract/material/packet/verifier/workspace/fmt/Clippy/policy validation.

## Non-goals

- No complete MaterialChangeMap; #975 owns the joined map.
- No model programme selection, proof ranking, final judgment or learned topology.
- No automatic rule acceptance or repository-wide prose ingestion.
- No live task or gate change.

## Completion

Close when one bounded current-revision architecture packet can be built from #968 contract facts plus #973/#974 mechanical scope, independently verified, and consumed by #975 without circular authority.

## Rollback

Keep the packet shadow-only and restore current shared context while retaining RepositoryContract and mechanical scope artifacts. Never resolve the cycle by duplicating architecture facts into a second map.

records.title: Backend: Category & tag system
records.body:
Define a category hierarchy and allow listings to be tagged. Support browsing and
filtering by category.

## What is broken today

`listings.category` is `varchar(50) NOT NULL` with **no constraint behind it**.
`validateListingInput` checks only that it is non-empty, the frontend's
`categorySchema` only caps it at 50 characters, and search filters with exact
string equality:

```go
if arg.Category != "" {
  b.WriteString(" AND listings.category = " + p)
}
```

So a seller typing `Mushrooms` and a seller typing `mushrooms` create two
categories that never match each other, and neither matches a buyer filtering on
`mushroom`. Nothing enumerates the valid values, so no client can render a
dropdown without hardcoding one — which is exactly what the seed does, with
`berries`, `greens`, `mushrooms`, `other` and `vegetables`.

This issue is therefore **partly a data migration**, not a greenfield feature.
Every listing already carries a category string that has to land somewhere.

## The categories half and #158

Making `listings.category` a foreign key means the frontend's free-text category
input would return 400 for anything but the five exact slugs. It does not today -
`AddListingSection`'s submit handler only `console.log`s, and listing creation
from the UI is blocked by #109 - so the backend PR is safe to merge on its own.

#158 replaces the field with a picker fed by `GET /categories`, and needs to land
**before #109**, not before the backend.

## Migration number

**`013`**. `009` is on `main`, `010` belongs to #16 (PR #154) and `011`/`012` to
#37 (PR #156). Both PRs should merge before this branch starts, or the numbering
goes out of order again — that cost us two `make db-reset` cycles on #37.

## Decisions needed before code

**1. A `categories` table, not a CHECK constraint**

CLAUDE.md's default for enums is `text` + `CHECK`, and that is right for closed
sets like order status. It cannot express a hierarchy, and this issue asks for
one — so a table is the exception rather than a departure. Recommend:

```
categories (id serial, slug text UNIQUE, name text, parent_id int NULL)
```

`slug` is the wire format (`mushrooms`), `name` is what a client displays. Follow
the `serial` half of the PK convention: categories are content, not people.

**2. One level of nesting, not arbitrary depth**

Recommend a top level and one level of children, enforced by a CHECK that a
category with a `parent_id` cannot itself be a parent. Arbitrary depth means
recursive CTEs for "show me everything under Mushrooms", and no forager needs
four levels. Easy to relax later; hard to un-ship.

**3. Keep `Listing.category` a slug string on the wire**

The listing response currently has `category: "mushrooms"`, and the frontend
reads it in `ListingCard`, `AddListingSection` and `api/types.ts`. Turning it
into an object breaks all three for no gain. Recommend `listings.category_id`
as the FK internally, with the response still publishing the **slug**, plus a
new `GET /categories` returning the tree for dropdowns and browse.

**4. Filtering by a parent should include its children**

Otherwise the hierarchy is decoration. `?category=mushrooms` returns listings in
`mushrooms` and in every child of it. This is the reason decision 2 matters — one
level makes it a single `IN` subquery instead of a recursive walk.

**5. Tags are free text, normalised, and capped**

Recommend a `tags (id, name UNIQUE)` table plus `listing_tags` as a composite-key
join, with tags lowercased and trimmed on write, and a cap of ~5 per listing.
Free text is the point — `chanterelle`, `roadside`, `organic` are not a set
anyone can enumerate in advance.

⚠️ **This is user-generated content with no moderation path**, the same gap
flagged in #16 for review text. A tag is short and public and attaches to
somebody else's search results. Worth deciding now whether tags need reporting,
or whether the cap plus normalisation is enough for a school project.

## Recommended split

Categories and tags are independent. Recommend doing them as **two commits or two
PRs on this issue** — categories first, since it carries the data migration and
the search change, tags second. Do not let one block the other's review.

## What already exists

- `listings.category` with five values in practice (see the seed)
- The search builder in `internal/database/listings_search.go`, which is
hand-written SQL rather than sqlc — the category filter lives there
- The pagination shape from `SearchListings`, reused twice since
- `GET /listings` documented in `openapi.yaml` with a `category` query param

## Scope

**Categories**

- [ ] Migration `013`: `categories` table, seeded with the five existing values;
    `listings.category_id` FK; backfill by matching `lower(category)`, with
    anything unmatched going to `other`; drop `listings.category`
- [ ] `GET /categories` — the tree, for dropdowns and browse
- [ ] Reject an unknown category on create/update with a 400, not a silent insert
- [ ] Filtering by a parent includes its children
- [ ] `Listing.category` keeps publishing the slug — no client change required

**Tags**

- [ ] Migration: `tags` + `listing_tags` (composite PK, no surrogate id)
- [ ] Attach and detach tags on a listing, capped and normalised
- [ ] `?tag=` filter on search
- [ ] Tags appear on the listing response

**Both**

- [ ] `openapi.yaml` in the same PR (`TestSpecMatchesRouter` fails otherwise)

## Testing

- The backfill leaves **no** listing without a category, including one whose
string matches nothing
- `Mushrooms` and `mushrooms` resolve to the same category
- An unknown category on create is a 400
- Filtering by a parent returns a child's listings; filtering by a child does not
return the parent's
- A tag cannot be attached twice to the same listing (the composite PK, not a
service check)
- Tag normalisation: ` Chanterelle ` and `chanterelle` are one tag
- The per-listing tag cap is enforced

## Out of scope

Species-level taxonomy (see the `species`

# Masck One Autonomous Production Queue

Single authoritative coordination queue for the autonomous Masck One production sprint. This issue is the live ownership lock, dependency ledger and release-control record. Do not create a second coordination issue.

## VERIFIED_MAIN
`cdcc6c5d7041a4b0d7594a7c8aa4fc58a8346207`

## CURRENT_DIGITAL_GATE
Iteration 16 Class-A provenance hardening is merged on verified main. Next critical path is dependency-safe realization of actuator frames/mount interfaces, continuous sweep/collision semantics, waste/fluid evidence contracts, then downstream packaging/retention/dry-bay integration. No digital representation may promote physical evidence.

## ACTIVE_PR_OWNERSHIP
| CELL | OWNER CELL | ACTIVE IMPLEMENTATION PR | OWNED_CAPABILITY | RELEASE STATE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Geometry / industrial-design CAD | none recorded | Iteration 17 actuator local frames + mount interfaces | READY TO START from verified main, subject to open-PR recheck |
| 3 | Mechanisms / wearable dynamics | none recorded | Continuous actuator sweep/collision contract downstream of Cell 2 | WAIT on Cell 2 interface contract; may build dependency-safe verification primitives only |
| 4 | Fluidics / packaging / electrical / thermal / hygiene | #23, head `b7f40426ecd64875305197bc14e30da7829fd89a` | waste cartridge capacity semantics, mixed-phase fault registry, orientation evidence contract | HOLD / REWORK |
| 5 | Independent verification / red-team | review lane, no implementation ownership | exact-head provenance + collision + evidence-state attack | ACTIVE review authority |
| 1 | Conductor / integration | no competing specialist implementation PR | release control, dependency contracts, queue, integration fixes | ACTIVE |

## PR_23_RELEASE_DECISION
Exact-head GitHub `engineering-integrity` CI succeeded on `b7f40426ecd64875305197bc14e30da7829fd89a`, but Cell 5 found a material provenance defect. `WasteArchitecture.validate()` validates `source_main_sha` format only, so a syntactically valid stale historical SHA can be accepted as current provenance. Existing adversarial coverage checks malformed identity, not valid-but-stale identity. Therefore PR #23 is **NOT MERGEABLE** despite green CI.

Required repair on the existing Cell-4 branch, not a new PR:
1. Add an explicit expected-upstream identity contract at validation/release time.
2. Reject a different valid 40-hex SHA adversarially.
3. Apply equivalent current-release binding to authority revision where the object claims current authority consumption.
4. Preserve historical provenance metadata if useful, but separate provenance recording from freshness validation.
5. Do not claim arbitrary `evidence_id` text is sufficient physical-evidence provenance. Future verified evidence ingestion must bind evidence identity/revision cryptographically.
6. Rerun full exact-head CI after repair. Cell 5 must re-review the revised head before Cell 1 merge decision.

## DEPENDENCY_GRAPH
`verified main / Iteration 16` -> `Cell 2 actuator frames + mount interfaces` -> `Cell 3 continuous sweep/collision + coupling semantics` -> downstream structural/actuation integration.

`verified main / authority evidence discipline` -> `Cell 4 PR #23 provenance repair` -> waste route identities + pump-off/backflow topology -> cartridge insertion/service geometry when shell/retention interfaces exist.

Exterior/Class-A work may proceed only without inventing released aesthetic/manufacturing evidence and must preserve protected anatomy, nose/T-zone continuity and structural/service reservations.

## FORBIDDEN / EVIDENCE-GATED WORK
Do not promote airway safety, cleansing efficacy, fit/contact pressure, actuator performance, pump mixed-phase behavior, cartridge usable capacity, retention/release force, battery runtime/safety, WARM/COOL performance, hygiene/drying, manufacturing capability or human factors without the required supplier/material/bench/human/accredited evidence. records.title: fix: await Stage V dictionary persistence before indexing success
records.body:
## Problem

`LexiconBuilder.buildIncremental()` and `LexiconBuilder.backfill()` currently invoke `ITermDictionary.upsertEntries()` with `void`. The interface is asynchronous, so a delayed or rejected dictionary write is detached from the indexing operation. In the full-document path, Stage V can appear successful, the pipeline can return, and `AsyncJobRunner` can commit the already-open GraphDB batch before the dictionary rejection is observed.

The frozen production-runtime base for this issue is `bf42f7f95c256219cf88704a55e6cfa1a161b074` (`production-runtime`, including bounded indexing #7 and canonical passage metadata #8). The two fire-and-forget call sites are in `LexiconBuilder.buildIncremental()` and `LexiconBuilder.backfill()`.

## Authority and bounded contexts

- `LexiconBuilder` owns completion of the Stage V lexicon operation it starts.
- `ITermDictionary` / `SQLiteLexiconStore` own dictionary persistence. Their public signature remains `Promise<void>`.
- `FullDocumentIndexingPipeline` retains its existing mutation boundary: a Stage V failure inside the mutation `try` becomes `DocumentMutationError`.
- `AsyncJobRunner` remains the only owner of the GraphDB storage-batch lifecycle. It abandons an open/uncertain batch on `DocumentMutationError`; this issue does not add commit, retry, recovery, or WAL logic.
- Literature Hub acceptance observation belongs to downstream issue Ryuhei-So/literature-hub#245 and is not implemented here.

## Design packet

### Data flow and state

For each `buildIncremental` or `backfill` invocation, the only legal state sequence is:

```text
not_started -> local_transaction_running -> dictionary_settlement_pending
            -> settled -> returned
            -> failed  -> rejected
```

Within the existing synchronous `better-sqlite3` transaction, call the same injected dictionary exactly once with the same ordered entries and retain the returned Promise instead of discarding it. Preserve the current call position before thesaurus/ambiguity recomputation so successful SQLite behavior and derived rows do not reorder. The transaction returns both the current `LexiconBuildResult` and the retained settlement. Immediately after the transaction returns, await that exact settlement before returning the result. There is no retry, replacement Promise, detached callback, timeout, or fallback.

`SQLiteLexiconStore.upsertEntries()` must preserve synchronous SQLite failure propagation through the caller's active transaction while still returning `Promise<void>` on success: execute its existing synchronous transaction before returning an already-fulfilled Promise, rather than relying on an `async` function to convert a synchronous database exception into a detached rejection. This keeps production local rows atomic for synchronous SQLite failures without changing the interface or successful writes.

For a genuinely delayed alternate `ITermDictionary`, the local evidence transaction may already have committed before the Promise rejects. This issue does not invent cross-store two-phase commit. The operation still rejects before the full pipeline returns; the GraphDB batch is abandoned, the job is failed, and the existing delete-and-rebuild/replace semantics make a later explicitly authorized retry convergent. No retry is performed by this change.

### Invariants

- One invocation produces zero calls if existing logic has no call path, otherwise exactly one `upsertEntries` call and exactly one awaited settlement.
- No successful `LexiconBuildResult`, full-pipeline result, checkpoint, job completion, or GraphDB commit may occur before settlement fulfills.
- A settlement rejection is preserved as the cause. `FullDocumentIndexingPipeline` wraps it once in the existing `DocumentMutationError`; `AsyncJobRunner` abandons the unresolved storage batch, marks the job failed, and rethrows.
- `backfill()` propagates the original settlement failure and never reports a result early.
- Corpus ID, document ID, entries, order, timestamps, row contents, dictionary factory selection, Stage V enablement, and success result counts remain unchanged.
- Concurrent invocations gain no shared promise, global queue, or deduplication. Each invocation owns only its own settlement.

### Compatibility, privacy, and logging

- No schema or migration, public type change, payload observation, logging expansion, provider change, fallback, or production configuration change.
- Callers not using Stage V are byte-for-byte unaffected at the storage boundary.
- Successful SQLite-backed Stage V retains the same call count/order and end state.
- Errors continue through existing structured job failure paths; no entry payload is added to logs.

### Failure and rollback

- Synchronous SQLite throw: abort the active local transaction and reject.
- Immediately rejected or delayed Promise: reject before returning success; in the full pipeline this triggers existing fatal mutation handling and batch abandon.
- Lost/never-settling Promise: this issue does not invent an independent timeout. The owning caller's existing cancellation/deadline policy remains authoritative; a later timeout issue must be separate.
- Rollback is a code rollback with no data migration. Do not switch binaries while an indexing batch is active or recovery-pending: first use the current owner/runtime to abandon or recover, verify idle/WAL absent-or-zero, then roll back. Existing persisted lexicon rows remain schema-compatible.

## Adversarial acceptance tests

1. `buildIncremental` with a controllable delayed Promise stays pending, emits no result, and calls the dictionary once; it resolves only after that exact Promise resolves.
2. Immediate and delayed rejection both reject with the original cause; no second call, retry, fallback, or unhandled rejection occurs.
3. A synchronous SQLite failure from `SQLiteLexiconStore` aborts the enclosing local transaction; before/after relevant row projections are equal.
4. `backfill` has the same delayed

records.title: [Slice 09] Offline HTML architecture and diagnostics report
records.body:
## Parent PRD

#99

## What to build

Render ReconciliationReportV1 as a standalone offline HTML report with an architecture graph and a diagnostic investigation view. The report must make code-observed structure, documentation declarations, relations, evidence, documentation coverage, analyzer coverage and run metadata inspectable together.

## Type

AFK

## Scope and non-goals

This slice owns the deterministic reporter and browser interaction. It does not change discovery/reconciliation semantics, call a server, fetch remote assets at runtime, or integrate Archify. Reuse installed rendering dependencies where suitable.

## Implementation requirements

- Generate HTML only from a saved canonical report and embed or locally reference all required assets so the file works offline.
- Provide neutral architecture and diagnostic lenses with filters for severity, provenance, status, analyzer, entity and relation.
- Support search, stable anchors for entities/relations/diagnostics, upstream/downstream traversal and evidence navigation.
- Show unknown and not-analyzed coverage explicitly instead of hiding unsupported areas.
- Show paths, line ranges, hashes and bounded context by default; full source snippets require explicit opt-in configuration.
- Ensure malformed or incomplete artifacts render an actionable error page rather than silently displaying an incomplete graph.
- Keep graph semantics sourced from the canonical report; the browser must not recalculate relationships.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture report renders an offline HTML file that can be opened without a server or network connection.
- [ ] The architecture view displays packages/modules and their relations, and the diagnostic lens highlights findings and affected entities.
- [ ] Filters, search, stable anchors and upstream/downstream navigation work on the generated fixture.
- [ ] Evidence links expose the responsible path and line range without including snippets by default.
- [ ] HTML generation is deterministic for the same report artifact.
- [ ] Tests verify report rendering, required sections, offline asset behavior, snippet redaction and malformed input handling.

## Verification

Run: pnpm typecheck && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm build

The implementation is not complete until the command passes and the new tests cover the acceptance criteria.

## Blocked by

- Blocked by #103
- Blocked by #106

## User stories addressed

- User stories 64–73

## Definition of done

A developer can open one portable report and understand both the project architecture and the documentation/code mismatches.

Do not close or modify the parent PRD issue. Keep changes limited to this slice and update the parent linkage in the pull request description.
